microtheory.name: executable_memory_lifecycle
microtheory.definition: Composition pattern naming the primitives + invariants for managing executable code memory across compile, execute, invalidate, reclaim. Composed of: mmap'd PROT_EXEC pages with W^X enforcement, a bounded code cache with LRU eviction, epoch-based or hazard-pointer reclamation for safe concurrent freeing, explicit instruction-cache invalidation on write, safepoint maps for OSR transitions, and per-arena executable allocators. Each piece exists in other Mts (operating_systems' mmap + page protection; data_structures_algorithms' LRU + arena; realtime_systems' bounded GC + lock_free; computer_architecture's icache); this Mt names how they compose to give correct + bounded executable-memory lifecycle. Required by adaptive_tiered_dispatch (L2 dynamic), referenced by typed_graph_arena_layout (L1), instantiated by jit.rs.

concepts.name: executable_memory_lifecycle_pattern
concepts.definition: The composition pattern. Executable pages allocated via mmap(PROT_EXEC); managed under W^X (writable mapping aliases execute mapping); placed in a bounded code cache with LRU eviction; concurrent execution protected by epoch-based reclamation OR hazard pointers OR refcount per workload; explicit icache invalidation on write before execute; safepoint maps allow OSR back to the interpreter; eviction triggered by stale-epoch detection AND cache bound + LRU. Each lifecycle step has a named invariant; together they bound memory + prevent use-after-free + maintain icache coherency.

concepts.name: mmap_executable_pages
concepts.definition: Component 1. Code lives in mmap'd anonymous pages. Default permissions vary by platform: Linux allows PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC under capability (problematic — W^X violation), Apple Silicon requires MAP_JIT + pthread_jit_write_protect_np toggle, hardened Linux (PaX, SELinux) requires dual-mapping. Allocation granularity = page size (4K typically; 16K Apple Silicon; 2M huge pages for large code caches). Substrate analogue: dynasmrt::ExecutableBuffer wraps this.

concepts.name: write_xor_execute_enforcement
concepts.definition: Component 2. Pages are NEVER simultaneously writable AND executable. Mechanism options: (a) dual mapping — one virtual address maps PROT_WRITE, aliased address maps PROT_EXEC, write via the former + execute via the latter; (b) mprotect flipping — pages start writable, flip to PROT_EXEC after write; (c) Apple's MAP_JIT — per-thread toggle via pthread_jit_write_protect_np. Substrate analogue: jit.rs uses dynasmrt which handles per-platform.

concepts.name: icache_invalidation_after_write
concepts.definition: Component 3. After writing instruction bytes, the CPU's instruction cache must be invalidated for the affected range before the new code executes. x86: implicit on most cases (modified code rule), explicit clflush for safety. ARM/AArch64: REQUIRED via ic ivau + dsb ish + isb. Apple Silicon: implicit on the MAP_JIT toggle. Missing this on ARM causes stale-icache execution = undefined behaviour.

concepts.name: epoch_based_reclamation
concepts.definition: Component 4. crossbeam-epoch pattern. Each worker pins the current epoch on entering a JIT'd frame; epoch advances only when no worker holds an old epoch; freed-but-pinned artefacts queue for delayed free. Guarantees no use-after-free with O(1) per-call cost. Alternative to RCU + hazard pointers; trades steady-state memory for simpler API. Substrate analogue: planned in l2_adaptive integration.

concepts.name: hazard_pointers_alternative
concepts.definition: Component 5. Maged Michael 2004. Each thread publishes a small fixed-size array of pointers it's currently using; reclaimer scans all threads' hazard arrays before freeing. O(threads × hazards) overhead per free; constant memory overhead. Better than epoch-reclamation when threads outnumber long-lived references. Listed as alternative; substrate_rs picks epoch-based for the dispatcher workload.

concepts.name: refcount_arc_for_low_contention
concepts.definition: Component 6. Arc<ExecutableBuffer> for rules whose contention is low (rare-fire BestEffort). Avoids epoch-reclamation overhead when usage is sparse. Mixed approach: hot rules → epoch-reclaimed (no per-call atomic), cold rules → Arc (per-call atomic but simpler). Pattern chooses per-kind based on hot counter.

concepts.name: code_cache_bound
concepts.definition: Component 7. Total executable memory has a configurable byte limit. When inserting a new artefact would exceed the bound, the LRU policy evicts the least-recently-used artefact (refcount/epoch-protected freeing). Bound chosen relative to L1i + L2 cache sizes so the hot working set fits architecture caches. Zen 5 default: 4 MiB code cache (fits in L2 across 4 cores' worth).

concepts.name: lru_eviction_policy
concepts.definition: Component 8. Doubly-linked list + hashmap. On each artefact access, move to MRU position. On eviction, pop from LRU end. Eviction may be deferred until reclamation epoch advances (artefact still in use by worker). Substrate analogue: data_structures_algorithms' LRU_cache concept applied to compiled artefacts.

concepts.name: safepoint_map_for_osr
concepts.definition: Component 9. Per-JIT'd-rule map: native PC → equivalent interpreter Term-tree position + live variable layout. At guard failure or deopt request, the runtime consults the map at the current PC and reconstructs the interpreter state. Only PCs at named safepoints can deopt; the JIT inserts safepoint polls at loop back-edges + before calls. Substrate analogue: not yet in jit.rs; required for OSR.

concepts.name: patch_point_atomic_overwrite
concepts.definition: Component 10. For tier-up of an already-installed rule (replacing a slower JIT'd artefact with a faster one), a patch point in the trampoline allows atomic instruction overwrite. x86: 5-byte JMP is atomic if aligned. ARM: atomic 4-byte branch + dsb + isb. Patches happen at safepoints to avoid mid-instruction tearing.

concepts.name: compile_arena_pooling
concepts.definition: Component 11. dynasmrt ExecutableBuffer is one mmap per compile. Pooling reuses fixed-size slabs: each slab fits N typical-size artefacts; allocate by bump pointer; free by clearing the whole slab when all artefacts in it have been evicted. Cuts mmap churn ~10× for high tier-up rate. Substrate analogue: an arena allocator over executable pages; not yet in jit.rs.

concepts.name: per_thread_vs_shared_cache
concepts.definition: Component 12. Cache locality choice. Per-thread: no reader/writer coordination, but kind-K is compiled once per thread = duplicated memory + duplicated compile work. Shared: single compile, but readers need epoch/hazard/refcount discipline. Substrate analogue: shared with epoch-reclamation; the artefacts ARE the substrate's compiled rules — single source of truth.

concepts.name: no_use_after_free_under_concurrent_execution
concepts.definition: Invariant. A worker executing JIT'd code never has its PC invalidated by another worker's free. Enforced by reclamation discipline (epoch / hazard / refcount). Without this invariant, Γ-mutation-triggered eviction would crash workers mid-execution. THE load-bearing safety property of the entire dynamic dispatch system.

concepts.name: w_x_always_satisfied
concepts.definition: Invariant. No virtual page is simultaneously writable AND executable. Enforced per-platform (dual mapping, mprotect flip, MAP_JIT toggle). Required by hardened Linux + Apple Silicon; defence-in-depth on permissive platforms. Without this, JIT'd memory is a code-injection vector.

concepts.name: icache_coherent_with_dcache_at_execute
concepts.definition: Invariant. When control transfers to a JIT'd address, the icache reflects the bytes written by the compiler. Enforced via platform-specific icache flush before execute. Required on ARM/AArch64; defence-in-depth on x86. Without this, execution may run stale bytes.

concepts.name: bounded_total_executable_memory
concepts.definition: Invariant. Total bytes of mapped executable memory ≤ configured bound. Enforced by code_cache_bound + lru_eviction_policy. Required for embedded + RT contexts where unbounded code growth violates working-set sizing. Substrate's default 4 MiB fits Zen 5's L2.

concepts.name: osr_deopt_reconstructable
concepts.definition: Invariant. From any safepoint in JIT'd code, the runtime can reconstruct the equivalent interpreter state (Term-tree position + live values). Enforced by safepoint_map_for_osr + the JIT's safepoint placement discipline. Required for correctness of the interpreter-fallback invariant from adaptive_tiered_dispatch.

concepts.name: tradeoff_reclamation_scheme
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: epoch-based reclamation (low per-call cost, deferred memory reclamation, simpler API) vs hazard pointers (constant memory, but per-free O(threads × hazards) overhead) vs refcount (simple but per-call atomic cost). substrate_rs: epoch for hot, Arc for cold; per-kind choice.

concepts.name: tradeoff_w_x_mechanism
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: dual mapping (write + execute aliases, supports lock-free concurrent JIT, ~2× VA usage) vs mprotect flipping (single mapping, slow syscall per flip, can't write during execute) vs MAP_JIT (Apple Silicon only, per-thread toggle, hardest to port). substrate_rs: dynasmrt picks platform default; advanced consumers can opt into dual mapping.

concepts.name: tradeoff_code_cache_size
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: large cache (more hot rules JIT'd → faster, more memory + cache pressure on L1i/L2) vs small cache (less memory but more frequent eviction → recompile thrash). Sweet spot: code cache ≈ L2 size per core. Substrate's 4 MiB default for Zen 5.

concepts.name: tradeoff_eviction_trigger
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: epoch-based (only stale entries evicted; bounded memory only if Γ mutates often) vs LRU + epoch (also evicts cold entries when bound exceeded; requires safe reclamation) vs cool-on-deopt (kind cooling demotes back to interpreter, frees aggressively). substrate_rs: epoch-staleness + LRU when bound exceeded; cool-on-deopt for high-deopt kinds.

concepts.name: tradeoff_per_thread_vs_shared
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: per-thread cache (no coordination, simpler, duplicated memory + compile work) vs shared cache (single compile, but readers need epoch/hazard discipline). Substrate: shared because the artefacts ARE the substrate's compiled rules — single source of truth matches Axiom 3.

concepts.name: substrate_rs_planned_instance
concepts.definition: substrate_rs canonical instance. l2_adaptive::CompiledCache<JittedFn> (planned) wraps the existing jit::JittedFn (which uses dynasmrt::ExecutableBuffer for mmap + W^X). Add epoch-based reclamation via crossbeam-epoch crate; add code_cache_bound + LRU; add icache_invalidation for AArch64 builds; add safepoint map. jit.rs currently handles mmap + per-platform W^X via dynasmrt; the lifecycle composition layers on top.

concepts.name: hotspot_codecache_reference
concepts.definition: HotSpot's CodeCache. Bounded executable memory pool divided into segments (non-method, non-profiled, profiled). Stop-the-world sweep evicts unreferenced compiled methods. ZGC + Shenandoah integrate. Reference architecture for code_cache_bound + lru_eviction. Influential design.

concepts.name: v8_codespace_reference
concepts.definition: V8's CodeSpace + CodeRange. Allocates JIT'd code in a contiguous 256 MiB region (CodeRange) for short jumps. Mark-sweep GC handles reclamation. Reference for compile_arena_pooling.

concepts.name: luajit_mcode_segments_reference
concepts.definition: LuaJIT mcode segments. 32K segments allocated as needed; never compacted; relies on traces being self-contained. Reference for compile_arena_pooling alternative (linear allocator without compaction).

concepts.name: webkit_jit_memory_reference
concepts.definition: WebKit's JIT memory model. Pre-allocated ExecutableMemoryPool with W^X via dual mapping on Apple Silicon. Reference for write_xor_execute_enforcement (especially dual-mapping pattern) + per_thread_vs_shared_cache (WebKit uses shared with locks).

concepts.name: linux_kernel_rcu_reference
concepts.definition: Linux kernel RCU. Read-Copy-Update for in-kernel lock-free reads with deferred reclamation. Inspiration for epoch_based_reclamation pattern (which is RCU's userspace cousin via crossbeam-epoch).

concepts.name: naming_makes_lifecycle_inspectable
concepts.definition: Meta. Before this Mt, executable-memory lifecycle was implicit: dynasmrt handled mmap, ExecutableBuffer's Drop handled munmap, no one named the concurrency story. Now: lifecycle is graph-resident — Jabberwock can answer 'how is my JIT memory managed?' by walking this Mt, finding components + invariants + canonical mechanism. Future memory issues become Mt revisions, not code archaeology.

concepts.name: this_mt_is_reused_across_design_layers
concepts.definition: Meta. This pattern is composed by adaptive_tiered_dispatch (L2 dynamic dispatch) AND will be composed by the future L5 JIT pattern AND is referenced by typed_graph_arena_layout (L1 — node arenas use a related-but-simpler version without the W^X concerns). Single source of truth for executable-memory lifecycle across the runner design.

rules.name: writing_jit_bytes_requires_w_x_discipline
rules.head: Jabberwock writes instruction bytes to mmap'd memory
rules.body: the bytes must be written via a writable mapping/state; before execution the memory must be transitioned to executable-only (mprotect, MAP_JIT toggle, or executed via aliased PROT_EXEC view). NEVER execute pages that are still writable; NEVER write pages that are currently executable from the same thread.

rules.name: freeing_jit_memory_requires_no_concurrent_execution
rules.head: Jabberwock evicts a compiled artefact while workers may be executing it
rules.body: the free must be deferred until ALL workers have advanced past the artefact's reclamation epoch (or all hazard pointers cleared, or refcount reached zero). Immediate free is use-after-free.

rules.name: writing_code_then_jumping_to_it_requires_icache_flush
rules.head: Jabberwock writes new instruction bytes then transfers control to them
rules.body: explicit icache invalidation is required on ARM/AArch64 between write and execute. x86 is implicit for most cases but defence-in-depth flush is cheap. Without this, execution may run stale instructions = undefined behaviour.

rules.name: eviction_under_pressure_must_respect_bounds
rules.head: Jabberwock's code cache exceeds its configured byte bound
rules.body: LRU eviction selects victim artefact + queues its free for the reclamation epoch. New artefact installed only after victim's memory is accounted as freed. Never overshoot the bound; never free in use.

rules.name: osr_requires_safepoint_polls
rules.head: Jabberwock compiles a rule and inserts JIT'd code for it
rules.body: the JIT must insert safepoint polls (loop back-edges + before calls + at guard checks) and emit a safepoint map (native PC → interpreter PC + live values). Without the map, deoptimisation cannot reconstruct interpreter state, and the correctness invariant breaks.

rules.name: patching_must_be_atomic_at_safepoint
rules.head: Jabberwock swaps a JIT'd artefact for a faster one in place
rules.body: the patch must happen at a safepoint (no executing thread is mid-instruction within the patch site) AND the patch must be a single atomic store (aligned 5-byte JMP on x86, aligned 4-byte branch on ARM). Mid-instruction patching is undefined.
